questions.question: What is a sitemap primarily useful for?
options: Publishing an inventory of candidate canonical URLs
Proving every listed page is high quality
Granting permission to ignore crawl policy
Guaranteeing that every URL still returns content

questions.question: What acquisition role do RSS and Atom feeds usually serve best?
options: Complete historical enumeration over all time
Incremental discovery of recent or updated items
Authorization for every linked private document
Exact deletion confirmation for missing entries

questions.question: Yesterday's sitemap has 100,000 URLs and today's has 100,500, including 500 new URLs. What should happen to the new entries?
options: Treat them as already fetched authoritative documents
Delete all earlier sitemap entries
Normalize, scope-check, and enqueue them as candidates
Assume they bypass robots and rate limits

questions.question: Version 7 update arrives after version 8. How should the sink prevent regression?
options: Apply every event strictly by arrival time
Delete version 8 before storing version 7
Treat both versions as one unordered text blob
Accept only a source version newer than the stored version

questions.question: Why combine push notifications with periodic inventory reconciliation?
options: Push provides low latency while inventory checks catch missed or inconsistent events
Inventory checks make idempotent notification handling unnecessary
Push delivery guarantees every event arrives exactly once and in order
Both channels always contain identical timestamps and deletion semantics

questions.question: What does an HTTP 304 response prove during a conditional sitemap fetch?
options: Every page listed in the sitemap remains unchanged
The sitemap resource itself was not modified under its validator
All previously missing URLs have been deleted
The crawler may skip future scope and robots checks

questions.topic: Search APIs as an Acquisition Channel
questions.question: What should a search API result set be treated as?
options: A complete guaranteed inventory of the web
A publisher-authorized corpus snapshot
A ranked discovery sample produced for a query
A permanent source-of-truth document store

questions.topic: Search APIs as an Acquisition Channel
questions.question: Why is cursor pagination often safer than offsets for changing results?
options: Cursors guarantee the provider index never changes
Cursors remove every quota and cost limit
Offsets preserve a stable snapshot by definition
Opaque continuation state reduces shifts caused by inserted results

questions.topic: Search APIs as an Acquisition Channel
questions.question: Three query variants each return 100 results but overlap heavily. What should be retained after URL deduplication?
options: Unique canonical URLs plus all query and rank provenance
Only the final query string and no discovery history
Three hundred duplicate documents as separate sources
Only snippets with the source URLs discarded

questions.topic: Search APIs as an Acquisition Channel
questions.question: Why should search snippets not normally become authoritative corpus text?
options: Snippets always contain the complete current document
They are query-biased, partial, and potentially stale
They cannot contain any words from the source page
They guarantee stronger licensing than fetched documents

questions.topic: Search APIs as an Acquisition Channel
questions.question: Which metric best reveals diminishing value from a query family?
options: Total provider result count before deduplication
Average character length of the query string
New unique eligible discoveries per additional request
The highest rank number returned on each page

questions.topic: Search APIs as an Acquisition Channel
questions.question: A provider returns HTTP 429. What is the correct response?
options: Rotate credentials to bypass the provider's limit
Increase concurrent requests until one succeeds
Treat the response as proof that the query has no results
Honor retry guidance, back off, and remain within quota

questions.topic: Seed Selection and Crawl Scope Policy
questions.question: What is a crawl seed?
options: A starting resource from which discovery traversal begins
A URL rejected after every crawl completes
A random document selected only for ranking evaluation
A database transaction containing all fetched pages

questions.topic: Seed Selection and Crawl Scope Policy
questions.question: When should a discovered URL be checked against scope?
options: Only after its content has entered the production index
Before it enters the fetch frontier, and again after redirects
Only when its response exceeds the size limit
After all linked hosts have been crawled

questions.topic: Seed Selection and Crawl Scope Policy
questions.question: Why is dropping every query parameter unsafe?
options: All parameters are tracking noise and never identify content
It guarantees infinite duplicate URLs
Semantic parameters such as version can identify different resources
Scope rules cannot inspect normalized URLs

questions.topic: Seed Selection and Crawl Scope Policy
questions.question: Why must redirect targets be scope-checked again?
options: Every redirect remains on the exact approved host
Redirects cannot point to private addresses
The source URL policy automatically authorizes any destination
An allowed source can redirect to an out-of-scope or unsafe target

questions.topic: Seed Selection and Crawl Scope Policy
questions.question: How should a new seed's value be evaluated?
options: Measure new canonical in-scope documents beyond existing seeds under a fixed budget
Count every duplicate URL as unique incremental coverage
Prefer seeds yielding only already-known navigation pages
Ignore host, path, language, and date distribution

questions.topic: Seed Selection and Crawl Scope Policy
questions.question: Why is broad crawling followed by deletion an unsafe scope strategy?
options: Deleted content was never technically fetched
Fetching itself can violate policy and expose systems to untrusted content
Downstream deletion always prevents request costs and rate-limit impact
Scope can only be applied after extraction has completed
